headline: Carney government's second budget projects $62.3B deficit with $142B in new spending
summary: The stories that stayed in the briefing most this week: Carney government's second budget projects $62.3B deficit with $142B in new spending; Alaska and Mississippi Senate races stay uncalled as Democrats widen leads; Brent dips below US$90 as Trump says Iran war could end 'fairly soon'.

top.headline: Carney government's second budget projects $62.3B deficit with $142B in new spending
top.what: Finance Minister Champagne tabled the budget Thursday: a $62.3-billion deficit for 2026-27 and about $142 billion in new spending over five years.
top.why: In the briefing on 6 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Alaska and Mississippi Senate races stay uncalled as Democrats widen leads
top.what: Democrats are projected to hold at least 259 House seats and at least 54 Senate seats; in the two uncalled Senate races, Democratic challengers lead by roughly 2,500 to 2,600 votes.
top.why: In the briefing on 6 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Brent dips below US$90 as Trump says Iran war could end 'fairly soon'
top.what: Oil fell to its lowest level since August after Trump said renewed U.S. strikes on Iran are quite unlikely, though Tehran denies any talks are under way and the U.S. naval blockade stays.
top.why: In the briefing on 6 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Thousands of Ontario students walk out over OSAP cuts: 'We can't afford rent'
top.what: Thousands of students walked out over OSAP changes and tuition, while a separate freeze on student aid at career colleges drags on with no restart date.
top.why: In the briefing on 6 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Toronto freezes most hiring as it faces a $1.1-billion budget gap
top.what: With Premier Ford ruling out a second 'New Deal', Toronto has paused most hiring to start closing a projected $1.1-billion shortfall in its 2027 budget.
top.why: In the briefing on 6 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Canada-U.S. trade talks continue as Democrats vow to repeal tariffs
top.what: Tariffs on Canadian goods remain while talks continue, and the DNC chair says Democrats would move to end them if they win power.
top.why: In the briefing on 5 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Canada loses 4,700 jobs in October; unemployment rises to 6.7%
top.what: Statistics Canada says employment slipped slightly in October and the jobless rate rose 0.2 points to 6.7%, its highest since April.
top.why: In the briefing on 4 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Trump names Stephen Miller White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles
top.what: Stephen Miller, the architect of Trump's immigration crackdown, starts today as White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. Trump also said he was only joking about offering UFC chief Dana White the press secretary job.
top.why: In the briefing on 4 of the last 7 days.
